items.text: 🚨 BREAKING 🚨 @RepLloydDoggett and I are calling on @HHSGov to ensure reasonable pricing for Xtandi, a prostate cancer drug developed with U.S. taxpayer dollars. Big Pharma is charging$190,000 for a year of treatment in the U.S., compared to $30,000 in other countries https://t.co/D3v4fZpFKC

My legislation would repeal the absurd mandate that requires the USPS to prefund 75 years’ worth of retiree healthcare benefits in just 10 years. It costs the agency at least $5 billion a year, and it has been responsible for a majority of their losses since 2013.

I also secured $3.5 million for the Port of Brookings Harbor Wastewater Treatment Plant. This project will help the Port improve compliance with state clean water standards – bettering our environment and supporting dozens of family wage jobs in Brookings. https://t.co/PELEYgspqU

Back in August, I visited the Benton County Crisis Respite Center, for which I’ve secured $ 1million. This center will divert individuals in crisis from the County jail and emergency room, helping them receive appropriate care for behavioral health. https://t.co/UIsNXPgytM https://t.co/v3qoojHpcX

Last night, I voted in support of legislation that brings nearly $18 million in investments to projects across southwestern Oregon. This funding will invest in our infrastructure, help combat wildfire, address homelessness, and better community health and clinics. https://t.co/AOCgEU0Cxm

Today we commemorate #Juneteenth, the oldest annual celebration of the end of slavery in the United States. Despite the end of slavery, the oppression of Black Americans has been built into every institution of American life from policing to health care. https://t.co/NTGbuby5R3

This morning, the Supreme Court decimated the constitutional right to abortion in its decision on Mississippi Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization. This is a devastating decision that undermines our representative democracy and the legitimacy of the Supreme Court.

In the aftermath of the Supreme Court’s disastrous ruling repealing the right to safe and accessible health care, the Senate must follow the House’s lead and take action to preserve the right to choose.

The Senate should waste no time and pass the Women’s Health Protection Act, which would codify the right to choose into federal law, and the Ensuring Access to Abortion Act, which would safeguard a women’s right to travel to another state to access reproductive health care.

We must also fund, strengthen, and extend mental health services and awareness so struggling individuals are more easily identified & able to get the help they need. A majority of Americans support stricter gun laws. I implore my Senate colleagues to pass this bill immediately.
